Study at a partner International partners International partners Study at a partner Internationalisation and partnership are at the heart of our corporate strategy. We have nurtured a diverse network of international partners overseas and value our reputation as a successful partnership institution. A diverse network of partners all over the globe We forged our first overseas transnational education collaboration in 1986. Thanks to this we are now engaged globally on programmes ranging over a variety of aspects. This range from staff and student exchanges, progression partners (articulations) to validated programmes. We also work in collaborative research, knowledge transfer and joint project ventures. We are proud to be at the forefront of higher education globalisation. We work in collaboration with governing bodies, ministries of education and international organisations. We provide staff and students with real-world international opportunities both at home and across the world. Awards 5 QS Stars (Excellent) for global engagement We’ve been awarded the maximum 5 QS Stars (Excellent) for global engagement and internationalisation (2025). We’re proud to be an international university, with a thriving staff and student community of over 38,000 people from over 100 countries. We offer a welcoming place for all our international students, encouraging you to become a global citizen. We support your success in study, with courses that lead to global career opportunities. Our 5 QS Stars also reflects the opportunities we give for you to experience other cultures. We're proudly connected with our overseas campus in Cyprus. We also have over 120 international partnerships with universities in China, Malaysia, the Far East, and more. Visit 5 QS Stars (Excellent) for global engagement International partner enquiries If you have a general enquiry, let us know and we'll pass it to the relevant team. Submit your enquiry Our international partners Open all accordion items Bangladesh Universal College Bangladesh (UCB) Universal College Bangladesh (UCB) is a pioneer in delivering international higher education programmes in Bangladesh. UCB is where excellence meets accessibility, and where every Bangladeshi student can have a world class educational experience leading to globally recognised qualifications. UCB’s aim is to give every student in Bangladesh the opportunity to get international qualifications from some of the world’s leading higher education institutions. UCB are the first transnational education (TNE) provider to be given all the relevant permissions by the Ministry of Education to offer international degree courses and pathway programmes, in the Country. UCB were recently approved by the Ministry of Education to deliver 3-year programmes in-country and will be delivering the following franchised programme for delivery from November 2024 at the UCB Dhaka city centre campus: BSc (Hons) Business and Marketing January 2025 and subject to validation* : BSc (Hons) Cyber Security* BSc (Hons) Software Engineering* UCB’s vision is as a world class education institution providing students the skills required to become work-ready professionals who can contribute to the social and economic development globally. Visit the UCB website Contact Phone: +880 1886-412222 / +880 1896-013882 / +880 1844-277342 / +880 1844-277343 Email: admission@ucbbd.org Address Universal College Bangladesh SA Tower, 1 Gulshan Avenue, Dhaka – 1212 Office Hours: 8:00 AM to 6pm BST (Saturday to Thursday) Egypt Arab Academy for Science, Technology and Maritime Transport (AASTMT) – El Alamein Campus The Arab Academy for Science, Technology and Maritime Transport (AASTMT) is located in El Alamein, Egypt and was established in 1972. For over 49 years, AASTMT has managed to keep up with the fast pace of development in the fields of education, training, consultation and scientific research. With its strong belief in the importance of Arab integration through enhancing joint Arab cooperation with the ultimate aim of attaining integrated Arab collaboration in all scientific fields, AASTMT has managed to accomplish further achievements in the fields of education, training and research. It has served the Arab community by providing education for both undergraduate and graduate students in over 35 specialisations. These include maritime transport, engineering, computers and information technology, international transport and logistics, management, language, media, law, pharmacy, fisheries and aquaculture technology, archaeology and finally dentistry and artificial intelligence. The institutional partnership with AASTMT enables students to access a wide range of our Engineering programmes through a dual degree partnership. Students can access the following programme titles once completed full study at El-Alamein Campus, Egypt. BSc (Hons) Mechanical Engineering BSc (Hons) Electronics and Communications Engineering BSc (Hons) Electrical Energy Engineering BSc (Hons) Construction Engineering BSc (Hons) Industrial and Management Engineering BSc (Hons) Architectural Engineering and Environmental Design BSc (Hons) Computer Engineering BSc (Hons) Aerospace and Aeronautical Engineering The partnership looks forward to announcing new developments and programme titles in the future ahead. Visit the AASTMT website . Contact Address: Arab Academy for Science, Technology & Maritime Transport El Alamein. Alamein Branch - El Alameen City El Alamein Matrouh Governorate European Universities in Egypt (EUE) The European Universities in Egypt (EUE) is established according to the presidential decree no.86 of the year 2021 and is based in the New Administrative Capital of Egypt. EUE is a higher education institution offering transnational education by bringing together reputable international universities to create a unique hub in the MENA region. Through partnerships with international universities, the EUE offers degree programmes in a diverse range of disciplines while granting its students the degree of the respective university. EUE will provide its students with state-of-the-art learning and research experiences to meet the needs of the emerging Egyptian economy and the international market. It aims to be a novel research hub that nurtures transnational education in the MENA region and makes a socio-economic impact across all collaborating markets. EUE aspires to be a distinguished and pioneering institution in higher education and scientific research. By hosting distinguished branches from world-ranked universities, EUE aims to graduate world-class students who will contribute to shape the future of their country and humanity. EUE campus aims to: Offer a safe and comfortable environment that assists students to excel and create; Endorse student learning through excellence in teaching support services and instructional delivery using both e-learning and traditional settings in response to current industry demands; and Foster an institutional culture that values diversity and cross-cultural competencies and skills identified by global industry experts. Four of the University of Lancashire's Engineering undergraduate programmes have been franchised for delivery from October 2021 at the brand new campus in New Cairo: BEng (Hons) Motorsport Engineering BEng (Hons) Mechatronics and Intelligent Machines BEng (Hons) Mechanical Engineering BEng (Hons) Electrical and Electronics Engineering BEng (Hons) Renewable and Sustainable Energy Engineering BEng (Hons) Civil Engineering BSc (Hons) Architectural Design BEng (Hons) Aerospace Engineering with Pilot Studies BEng (Hons) Aerospace Engineering BEng (Hons) Manufacturing Engineering BEng (Hons) Electronic Engineering The partnership is tied in with summer school, masters and PhD delivery at the Preston campus. Visit the EUE website Contact Phone: 16323 / +201029696399 / +201029695599 Email: info@EUE.edu.eg Address: Admissions Office: European Universities in Egypt 3rd Floor, Kira Building 367/3 Road 90 South (main road) (next to Top90 Mall/in front of Moon Valley Compound) New Cairo Egypt Campus Address: R3, New Administrative Capital, Egypt. Next to the Olympic City - Plus code: 2PR5+8H Cairo Governorate Desert - See on Google Maps . Greece College for Humanistic Sciences (ICPS), Greece The College for Humanistic Sciences (ICPS) is a longstanding partner of the University, responsible for delivering various franchise programmes. They are the only college in Greece to have been specialising in the science of human behaviour since 1989. Since the College was re-authorised by the Ministry of Education in 2013, it has made huge leaps in becoming a specialist institution in the field of human behaviour. The College is certified by the Pearson-Edexcel Training Center, the world’s largest professional certification body, and offers lifelong and distance programmes in Counselling, Learning Difficulties, and Counselling for Couples. Working alongside the Greek EFT Network, ICPS offer an array of approved programmes that meet the EFT Therapist criteria. This gives students the unique advantage of gaining double certification within the subject field, giving them a distinct advantage in their careers. Furthermore, ICPS trainers travel globally to do speeches and workshops. This includes speaking at the World Conference on Personal Counselling and Psychotherapy in New York. In July 2017, ICPS became a founding member of the Pan-Hellenic Association of Recognised Colleges. This means that the College plays a key role in the field of education in Greece and aspires to work with universities abroad. This initiative led to our current collaboration – we now offer MSc Applied Clinical Psychology and MSc Psychology (Conversion) courses which are based in Greece. Find out more about the College for Humanistic Sciences on their website . Contact Phone: +30.210.64.56.565 Email: reception@icps.edu.gr Address : 56a Filikon str. & Kanari 121 31 Agios Antonios, Peristeri Athens, Greece. Hong Kong (SAR) City University of Hong Kong, School of Continuing & Professional Education (SCOPE) Our partners at the School of Continuing and Professional Education (SCOPE) at City University in Hong Kong offer courses related to Fire Engineering, Fire Safety Engineering, English for International Corporate Communication and International Business Communication. Their fire safety programmes have been developed to serve the needs of the Hong Kong Fire Services Authority. Since its development in 1991, SCOPE has been a pioneer and major provider of quality professional education and training in Hong Kong. The School offers a range of programmes at different levels. Their bachelor’s degree programmes focus on professional education in a variety of disciplines. Their postgraduate programmes are specialist, delivering academically sound and career-relevant content which meets the needs of surrounding communities and reflects ongoing social and technological changes. Over the past two decades, the School has worked alongside us to provide bachelor’s degrees to a high standard, ensuring that we are developing knowledgeable and highly employable graduates within key sectors. Franchised courses: BA (Hons) English for International Corporate Communication BA (Hons) International Business Communication (with Japanese/Chinese) Foundation Fire Safety Engineering BEng (Hons) Fire Engineering MSc Fire Safety Engineering MSc Fire Scene Investigation Find out more about SCOPE on their website . Contact Phone: 00 852 3442 7423 Email: scope@cityu.edu.hk Address: 2410, 2/F, Li Dak Sum Yip Yio Chin Academic Building (LI) City University of Hong Kong Tat Chee Avenue, Kowloon Hong Kong Hong Kong College of Technology, (Hong Kong Institute of Higher Education) We have enjoyed a very successful relationship with the Centre of International Education at Hong Kong College of Technology (HKCT) since 2005. The initial collaboration was in the areas of construction project management, facilities management and marketing. Our courses have greatly benefited industries throughout Hong Kong. HKCT and its predecessor, Mong Kok Workers’ Night School, was formed with the aim of addressing large-scale redundancies and educational problems in post-war Hong Kong. For more than 70 years, its mission and ethos have evolved continuously to adapt to the changing demands of society (from literacy education at Mong Kok Workers’ Night School in the 1940s and 1950s and school skill labour training in the 1960s, to professional education in the 1970s and 1980s, and retraining in the 1990s). Their programmes now extend to post-secondary education, including the delivery of outstanding academic degrees. In 2014, HKCT Institute of Higher Education was approved by the Chief Executive in-Council as it became the nineteenth degree-awarding higher education institution in Hong Kong. HKCT is committed to professional career education and delivers a variety of programmes, including full-time and part-time degrees and diplomas, with an emphasis on applied skills and meeting the labour demands of Hong Kong’s industries – to date they have provided over 600,000 qualified students. Franchised programmes: BSc (Hons) Construction Project Management BSc (Hons) Facilities Management MSc Construction Project Management Find out more about Hong Kong College of Technology on their website . Contact Phone: 00 852 2926 1222 Email: enquiry@hkct.edu.hk Address: 14 Princess Margaret Road Homantin, Kowloon Hong Kong School for Higher and Professional Education (SHAPE), Vocational Training Council, Hong Kong The Vocational Training Council (VTC) is the largest training provider in Hong Kong. We have been working with the VTC for many years and now offer a wide range of courses in Engineering related subjects. The School for Higher and Professional Education (SHAPE) is a member institution of the VTC. Since its establishment in 2003, SHAPE has been providing quality top-up degree programmes in a wide range of professions by working closely with partner institutions. Through collaborating with us and many other universities across the world, graduates will earn a reputable and recognised top-up degree in Hong Kong. Both full-time and part-time study options are available to suit the needs of every student. In the academic year 2020-21, some 44 accredited programmes are pitched at Level 5 under the Hong Kong Qualifications Framework. SHAPE offers programmes in Engineering and other areas, including Applied Science; Business; Childcare; Elderly and Community Services; Design; Hospitality, Tourism and Leisure; and Information Technology. Franchised programmes: BSc (Hons) Building Surveying BSc (Hons) Quantity Surveying BEng (Hons) Building Services and Sustainable Engineering BSc (Hons) Architectural Studies Contact Phone: 00 852 25952771 Email: shape@vtc.edu.hk Address: SHAPE Central Office Room 008, Academic Block 30 Shing Tai Road, Chai Wan, Hong Kong Malaysia IMU University The International Medical University (IMU) is Malaysia’s first and most established private medical and healthcare university, with more than 25 years of dedicated experience in healthcare education. IMU is also the first university in Malaysia to offer both conventional and complementary medicine under one institution. Established in 1992, IMU was the first private higher education institution in Malaysia authorised to confer academic degrees, and it was granted full university status by the Malaysian government in 1999. IMU offers a wide range of undergraduate and postgraduate programmes across medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, health sciences, and complementary medicine, delivered through modern teaching facilities, laboratories, clinical training centres, and strong partnerships with healthcare providers. Students who meet the published entry criteria for the articulation arrangement may be eligible to progress to the MBBS (Hons) (Bachelor of Medicine & Bachelor of Surgery) Year 3 Entry. Programme availability, entry requirements, and progression routes are kept under review and may change. The partnership looks forward to sharing any future developments and additional programme options as they are confirmed. Visit International Medical University Website SEGi University, Malaysia SEGi University and Colleges first opened its doors as Systematic College in 1977 in the heart of Kuala Lumpur’s commercial district, offering globally recognised professional qualifications. Since then, SEGi has experienced significant growth by adapting and catering to an increasing demand for tertiary education and professional qualifications in Malaysia. We are proud to have SEGi University as our partners in Malaysia. A leading private higher education institution, they deliver innovative programmes to cater to the needs of industry and the wider community, nationally and internationally. We have collaborated on a suite of courses designed to equip students with highly employable skills and knowledge. When students graduate they receive a double degree qualification – which means they receive certification from both ourselves and SEGi to demonstrate their expertise and enhance their employment prospects. The courses we deliver collaboratively with SEGi include: BA (Hons) Education BEng (Hons) Engineering BA (Hons) Hospitality Management BSc (Hons) Information Technology BA (Hons) International Business Administration BA (Hons) International Accounting BA (Hons) International Accounting and Finance BA (Hons) Mass Communications BA (Hons) Public Relations with English Find out more about SEGi University on their website . Contact Phone: 00 603 6145 1777 Email: infokd@segi.edu.my Address: SEGi University Jalan Teknologi Kota Damansara 47810 Petaling Jaya Selangor, Malaysia Mauritius UOM Enterprise Ltd UOM Enterprise Ltd was created in 2010 by the University of Mauritius Trust and is registered as a post-secondary educational institution. We entered a partnership with UOME in 2011 to deliver numerous courses in Mauritius. UOME was established by the UOM Trust (a charitable trust set up by the University of Mauritius) to respond to the training needs of the African continent. They boast brand new teaching facilities, providing top-class programmes for ambitious students. Our LLM in International Business Law has been operating within Mauritius since 2011 and the curriculum has been highly praised by the professional law community as an outstanding source of skills and knowledge for students. In order to diversify the programme on offer in Mauritius, and after three years of delivering an LLM in International Business Law, we worked alongside UOME to launch various undergraduate and postgraduate courses within the fields of Law and Construction in 2014. All of them have gone through the rigorous process of accreditation by the TEC and the Quality Assurance Agency for Higher Education to provide students with fully recognised qualifications. In 2019, we celebrated a record number of students graduating from UOME across a range of courses. There were more students than ever graduating from our LLB and LLM programmes and, for the first time, there were students graduating from our Graduate Diploma in Law (GDL). In addition, there were a number of graduates from the MSc in Construction Project Management. Contact Phone: 00 230 467 8925/00 230 467 8926 Email: contactus@uomenterprise.ac.mu Address: 1st Floor, Blue Tower, Rue de L'Institut Ebène Mauritius Oman International College of Engineering and Management, Oman The International College of Engineering and Management (ICEM) is at the forefront of educational excellence in the Sultanate of Oman. This renowned higher education college offers students an unrivalled combination of practical courses led by experts and delivering educational excellence. The International College of Engineering and Management (ICEM) is an educational beacon that brings together outstanding students from many different countries. Our partnership with ICEM has existed for over ten years, delivering unique degree courses in Fire Safety Engineering, Well Engineering, Facilities Management and Health, Safety and Environmental Management. Together, we strive to offer an unrivalled educational experience, with opportunities to network with a truly international body of students and staff. Our courses are practical, producing industry-ready graduates and informed research. ICEM continue to provide our approved courses in Oman, focusing on providing a truly world-class higher education learning environment based on practical vocational teaching with a strong bias towards producing graduates who are ‘employer ready’, well rounded and internationally experienced. There have been countless graduates from ICEM with diplomas and degrees accredited by the University of Lancashire. The vast majority have entered the private sector and gone on to enjoy successful careers in Oman and other Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. Contact Phone: 00 968 24512000/2020 Email: info@icem.edu.om Address: International College of Engineering and Management PO Box 2511, CPPO Seeb PC11 Muscat, Oman People’s Republic of China Beijing Institute of Technology (BIT), China We have enjoyed a longstanding partnership with Beijing Institute of Technology (BIT) in China for over 20 years. During this time we have collaborated on a number of successful Electronic and Engineering programmes, including the renowned BEng (Hons) Electronic Engineering course. Established in 1940, Beijing Institute of Technology (BIT) is a major science and engineering university which is now affiliated to China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. BIT has become a key research institution in the aftermath of the Chinese government’s nationwide Project 211, Project 985 and ‘Top A World-class University’ strategies, which saw major investment in the country’s higher education institutions, with a view to delivering future social development and economic growth. BIT aspires “to develop students as leaders with ambition, wisdom, innovation and sense of duty.” A pioneer in the fields of science, technology and education, BIT has been called upon to develop strategies which address national and global needs. Today the Institute is recognised as a leader in technologies relating to intelligent and bionic robotics, space adaptive optics, green energy, modern communications and industrial process control. BIT comprises 18 professional schools as well as a number of key research institutes, including Xu Teli School; Advanced Research Institute for Multidisciplinary Science; the Institute of Advanced Structure Technology; and the Institute of Convergence Medical and Engineering. The following subjects at BIT are ranked in the top 1% of the Essential Science Indicators (ESI) international disciplines: Chemistry, Computer Science, Engineering, Material Science, Mathematics, Physics, and Social Sciences. Visit the Beijing Institute of Technology website . Contact Phone, Office of International Students: 00 86-10-68918316 00 86-13910172716 Email: wangying318@gmail.com , yingwang@bit.edu.cn Address: Beijing Institute of Technology 5 Zhongguancun Nandajie, Haidian District 100081 Beijing, PR China Guangdong University of Foreign Studies, China Since 1986, we have enjoyed a successful partnership with the Guangdong University of Foreign Studies in China. Our collaboration focuses on International Business and International Journalism, and has remained strong and successful in providing students with amazing opportunities over the years. Guangdong University of Foreign Studies (GDUFS) has the mission of “whole-person education and pursuit of excellence” and pursues the internationalisation of its faculty, students, academic research and management, with a view to being recognised as a high-tier internationalised university of excellence. GDUFS has three beautiful campuses: the main campus, the North Campus at the foot of the Baiyun Mountain; the South Campus in Guangzhou High Education Mega Center; and Dalang Campus. The University offers more than 70 programmes in art, economics, education, engineering, law, literature, management and science. They pride themselves in being able to offer a wide variety of language programmes, with 26 foreign languages currently available. GDUFS is one of just 19 universities worldwide qualified to provide high-end translation professionals to the United Nations and the only foreign studies-oriented university in the CAMPUS Asia programme. It is a member of the International Standing Conference of University Institutes of Translators and Interpreters (CIUTI), International Federation of Translators (FIT) and the founder of World Interpreter and Translator Training Association (WITTA). The University is active in a full range of international co-operation and exchanges in education. Study at a partner International partners International partners Study at a partner Internationalisation and partnership are at the heart of our corporate strategy. We have nurtured a diverse network of international partners overseas and value our reputation as a successful partnership institution. A diverse network of partners all over the globe We forged our first overseas transnational education collaboration in 1986. Thanks to this we are now engaged globally on programmes ranging over a variety of aspects. This range from staff and student exchanges, progression partners (articulations) to validated programmes. We also work in collaborative research, knowledge transfer and joint project ventures. We are proud to be at the forefront of higher education globalisation. We work in collaboration with governing bodies, ministries of education and international organisations. We provide staff and students with real-world international opportunities both at home and across the world. Awards 5 QS Stars (Excellent) for global engagement We’ve been awarded the maximum 5 QS Stars (Excellent) for global engagement and internationalisation (2025). We’re proud to be an international university, with a thriving staff and student community of over 38,000 people from over 100 countries. We offer a welcoming place for all our international students, encouraging you to become a global citizen. We support your success in study, with courses that lead to global career opportunities. Our 5 QS Stars also reflects the opportunities we give for you to experience other cultures. We're proudly connected with our overseas campus in Cyprus. We also have over 120 international partnerships with universities in China, Malaysia, the Far East, and more. Study at a partner International partners International partners Study at a partner Internationalisation and partnership are at the heart of our corporate strategy. We have nurtured a diverse network of international partners overseas and value our reputation as a successful partnership institution. A diverse network of partners all over the globe We forged our first overseas transnational education collaboration in 1986. Thanks to this we are now engaged globally on programmes ranging over a variety of aspects. This range from staff and student exchanges, progression partners (articulations) to validated programmes. We also work in collaborative research, knowledge transfer and joint project ventures. We are proud to be at the forefront of higher education globalisation. We work in collaboration with governing bodies, ministries of education and international organisations. We provide staff and students with real-world international opportunities both at home and across the world. Awards 5 QS Stars (Excellent) for global engagement We’ve been awarded the maximum 5 QS Stars (Excellent) for global engagement and internationalisation (2025). We’re proud to be an international university, with a thriving staff and student community of over 38,000 people from over 100 countries. We offer a welcoming place for all our international students, encouraging you to become a global citizen. We support your success in study, with courses that lead to global career opportunities. Our 5 QS Stars also reflects the opportunities we give for you to experience other cultures. We're proudly connected with our overseas campus in Cyprus. We also have over 120 international partnerships with universities in China, Malaysia, the Far East, and more. Visit 5 QS Stars (Excellent) for global engagement International partner enquiries If you have a general enquiry, let us know and we'll pass it to the relevant team. Working alongside the Greek EFT Network, ICPS offer an array of approved programmes that meet the EFT Therapist criteria. Study at a partner International partners International partners Study at a partner Internationalisation and partnership are at the heart of our corporate strategy. We have nurtured a diverse network of international partners overseas and value our reputation as a successful partnership institution. A diverse network of partners all over the globe We forged our first overseas transnational education collaboration in 1986. Thanks to this we are now engaged globally on programmes ranging over a variety of aspects. This range from staff and student exchanges, progression partners (articulations) to validated programmes. We also work in collaborative research, knowledge transfer and joint project ventures. We are proud to be at the forefront of higher education globalisation. We work in collaboration with governing bodies, ministries of education and international organisations. We provide staff and students with real-world international opportunities both at home and across the world. Awards 5 QS Stars (Excellent) for global engagement We’ve been awarded the maximum 5 QS Stars (Excellent) for global engagement and internationalisation (2025). We’re proud to be an international university, with a thriving staff and student community of over 38,000 people from over 100 countries. We offer a welcoming place for all our international students, encouraging you to become a global citizen. We support your success in study, with courses that lead to global career opportunities. Our 5 QS Stars also reflects the opportunities we give for you to experience other cultures. We're proudly connected with our overseas campus in Cyprus. We also have over 120 international partnerships with universities in China, Malaysia, the Far East, and more. Visit 5 QS Stars (Excellent) for global engagement International partner enquiries If you have a general enquiry, let us know and we'll pass it to the relevant team. Through partnerships with international universities, the EUE offers degree programmes in a diverse range of disciplines while granting its students the degree of the respective university. Greece College for Humanistic Sciences (ICPS), Greece The College for Humanistic Sciences (ICPS) is a longstanding partner of the University, responsible for delivering various franchise programmes. They are the only college in Greece to have been specialising in the science of human behaviour since 1989. Since the College was re-authorised by the Ministry of Education in 2013, it has made huge leaps in becoming a specialist institution in the field of human behaviour. The College is certified by the Pearson-Edexcel Training Center, the world’s largest professional certification body, and offers lifelong and distance programmes in Counselling, Learning Difficulties, and Counselling for Couples. Working alongside the Greek EFT Network, ICPS offer an array of approved programmes that meet the EFT Therapist criteria. This gives students the unique advantage of gaining double certification within the subject field, giving them a distinct advantage in their careers. Furthermore, ICPS trainers travel globally to do speeches and workshops. This includes speaking at the World Conference on Personal Counselling and Psychotherapy in New York. In July 2017, ICPS became a founding member of the Pan-Hellenic Association of Recognised Colleges. This means that the College plays a key role in the field of education in Greece and aspires to work with universities abroad. This initiative led to our current collaboration – we now offer MSc Applied Clinical Psychology and MSc Psychology (Conversion) courses which are based in Greece. Find out more about the College for Humanistic Sciences on their website . Study at a partner International partners International partners Study at a partner Internationalisation and partnership are at the heart of our corporate strategy. We have nurtured a diverse network of international partners overseas and value our reputation as a successful partnership institution. A diverse network of partners all over the globe We forged our first overseas transnational education collaboration in 1986. Thanks to this we are now engaged globally on programmes ranging over a variety of aspects. This range from staff and student exchanges, progression partners (articulations) to validated programmes. We also work in collaborative research, knowledge transfer and joint project ventures. We are proud to be at the forefront of higher education globalisation. We work in collaboration with governing bodies, ministries of education and international organisations. We provide staff and students with real-world international opportunities both at home and across the world. Awards 5 QS Stars (Excellent) for global engagement We’ve been awarded the maximum 5 QS Stars (Excellent) for global engagement and internationalisation (2025). Our 5 QS Stars also reflects the opportunities we give for you to experience other cultures. We're proudly connected with our overseas campus in Cyprus. We also have over 120 international partnerships with universities in China, Malaysia, the Far East, and more. With transformative clinical opportunities in the United States, United Kingdom and abroad, our students develop an in-depth understanding of different healthcare systems and diverse patient populations. This is a four-year programme with the first two years focused on studying the medical sciences and understanding how to integrate foundational knowledge with clinical practice. The final two years are spent completing core clinical clerkships across AUC School of Medicine’s wide network of affiliated teaching hospitals. Study at a partner International partners International partners Study at a partner Internationalisation and partnership are at the heart of our corporate strategy. We have nurtured a diverse network of international partners overseas and value our reputation as a successful partnership institution. A diverse network of partners all over the globe We forged our first overseas transnational education collaboration in 1986. Thanks to this we are now engaged globally on programmes ranging over a variety of aspects. This range from staff and student exchanges, progression partners (articulations) to validated programmes. We also work in collaborative research, knowledge transfer and joint project ventures. We are proud to be at the forefront of higher education globalisation. We work in collaboration with governing bodies, ministries of education and international organisations. We provide staff and students with real-world international opportunities both at home and across the world. Awards 5 QS Stars (Excellent) for global engagement We’ve been awarded the maximum 5 QS Stars (Excellent) for global engagement and internationalisation (2025). Our 5 QS Stars also reflects the opportunities we give for you to experience other cultures. We're proudly connected with our overseas campus in Cyprus. We also have over 120 international partnerships with universities in China, Malaysia, the Far East, and more. Study at a partner International partners International partners Study at a partner Internationalisation and partnership are at the heart of our corporate strategy. We have nurtured a diverse network of international partners overseas and value our reputation as a successful partnership institution. A diverse network of partners all over the globe We forged our first overseas transnational education collaboration in 1986. We also work in collaborative research, knowledge transfer and joint project ventures. We are proud to be at the forefront of higher education globalisation. We work in collaboration with governing bodies, ministries of education and international organisations. We provide staff and students with real-world international opportunities both at home and across the world. Study at a partner International partners International partners Study at a partner Internationalisation and partnership are at the heart of our corporate strategy. Study at a partner International partners International partners Study at a partner Internationalisation and partnership are at the heart of our corporate strategy. We have nurtured a diverse network of international partners overseas and value our reputation as a successful partnership institution. A diverse network of partners all over the globe We forged our first overseas transnational education collaboration in 1986. Thanks to this we are now engaged globally on programmes ranging over a variety of aspects. This range from staff and student exchanges, progression partners (articulations) to validated programmes. We also work in collaborative research, knowledge transfer and joint project ventures. We are proud to be at the forefront of higher education globalisation. We work in collaboration with governing bodies, ministries of education and international organisations. We provide staff and students with real-world international opportunities both at home and across the world. Awards 5 QS Stars (Excellent) for global engagement We’ve been awarded the maximum 5 QS Stars (Excellent) for global engagement and internationalisation (2025). We’re proud to be an international university, with a thriving staff and student community of over 38,000 people from over 100 countries. We offer a welcoming place for all our international students, encouraging you to become a global citizen. We support your success in study, with courses that lead to global career opportunities. Our 5 QS Stars also reflects the opportunities we give for you to experience other cultures. We're proudly connected with our overseas campus in Cyprus. We also have over 120 international partnerships with universities in China, Malaysia, the Far East, and more. They are the only college in Greece to have been specialising in the science of human behaviour since 1989. Since the College was re-authorised by the Ministry of Education in 2013, it has made huge leaps in becoming a specialist institution in the field of human behaviour. The College is certified by the Pearson-Edexcel Training Center, the world’s largest professional certification body, and offers lifelong and distance programmes in Counselling, Learning Difficulties, and Counselling for Couples. Working alongside the Greek EFT Network, ICPS offer an array of approved programmes that meet the EFT Therapist criteria. This gives students the unique advantage of gaining double certification within the subject field, giving them a distinct advantage in their careers. Furthermore, ICPS trainers travel globally to do speeches and workshops. This includes speaking at the World Conference on Personal Counselling and Psychotherapy in New York. In July 2017, ICPS became a founding member of the Pan-Hellenic Association of Recognised Colleges. This means that the College plays a key role in the field of education in Greece and aspires to work with universities abroad. This initiative led to our current collaboration – we now offer MSc Applied Clinical Psychology and MSc Psychology (Conversion) courses which are based in Greece. How to apply as an international student International students Are you an international student thinking about studying at a UK university? See our information about how to apply, including entry requirements, the visa process, and bursaries and scholarships. Expert advice for international students If you’re an international student looking to study in the UK, contact the representative in your country for advice. They will be available to offer expert advice, guidance and support to help you with your application. Find your country representative How to apply for an undergraduate course in the UK If you’re from outside the UK and want to study with us, you can make your application one of two ways – either via the Universities and Colleges Admissions Service (UCAS) or via our online applications portal . Before submitting your application, you should first check the specific entry requirements for the course in relation to your home country or place of study, as well as the English language requirements, to ensure you are eligible. For those within the EU, you should apply via UCAS rather than directly. UCAS online application UCLan online application system If you are experiencing any issues with completing the online application form, or if you have any questions in relation to your application, please email the International Team inbox . Thinking of applying for medicine? We have put together some guidance to help you with your application. If you do not meet the entry requirements for a course, you could complete a foundation programme with OnCampus or another of our recognised international foundation providers . This will allow you to progress onto a degree at the university. Read more about How to apply for an undergraduate course in the UK How to apply for a postgraduate course in the UK If you're looking to start your postgraduate application and you're from outside the UK, you can apply for our postgraduate courses via our online application portal . You’ll simply need to create an account and work through the application steps as indicated. In general, our postgraduate programmes require a minimum of a lower second class degree from a recognised university, or a professional qualification deemed to be equivalent. In some cases you will need to submit a proposal as part of your degree. Before starting your online application, you should first check the entry requirements and English language requirements in relation to your home country or place of study to ensure you are eligible. Online application If you are experiencing any issues with completing the online application form, or have any questions about the application process, please contact international@uclan.ac.uk Read more about How to apply for a postgraduate course in the UK How to apply for postgraduate research in the UK We have an established research reputation in a wide range of academic disciplines and on completion of your research degree, you should be in a very strong position for pursuing your chosen career. Find out more about how to apply for postgraduate research in the UK . English language entry requirements We accept a range of English language qualifications including IELTS, TOEFL and Pearson Test of English. We can also accept some country specific qualifications. What we can accept as proof of English language level can vary depending on level of study and sometimes the course. For the general English language requirements we accept, please take a look at our English entry requirements webpage . If you would like to check whether we can accept local qualifications, please check your country or region’s entry requirements page . Read more about English language entry requirements Important dates for international applicants Please view our admission deadlines for international applicants below September 2026 dates September 2026 dates Application deadline : 19 July 2026 Deposit deadline : 16 August 2026 Take a virtual tour Can't make it onto campus but want to explore the university? Discover our course facilities, social spaces, accommodation and city hot spots on our virtual tour. Explore our campuses Further information The University of Central Lancashire is a diverse environment, which brings people into contact with each other in a wide variety of ways. The University community includes students who are children (those under the age of 18) and vulnerable adults. We have a duty to safeguard these groups of individuals, as well as a duty to provide a safe environment in which our staff can work and all of our students can study and where relevant, live. We therefore ask all applicants who have accepted a place with us if they have relevant unspent criminal convictions obtained in the UK or other jurisdiction. This is so that we can consider the implications of any convictions, assess any risks to you or others within the University environment and determine whether we can reasonably manage any risks to enable you to take up your place here. Having a relevant unspent conviction therefore is not an automatic barrier to taking up your place on your chosen programme. Therefore, if you accept an offer the University will ask you to disclose details about relevant unspent convictions and supporting information. Research Research and Knowledge Exchange Service (RKES) Research and Knowledge Exchange Service (RKES) Research Our skilled and knowledgeable staff provide a professional, effective and holistic offering for researchers to support them in their research and enterprise journey, from ideas and training to funding, dissemination and knowledge exchange. The service comprises six units : Enterprise and Engagement Unit (EEU) Ethics, Integrity and Governance Unit (EIGU) Graduate Research School (GRS) Grants and Funding Unit (GFU) Impact and Outputs Unit (IOU) Intellectual Property and Commercialisation Unit (IPU) Enterprise and Engagement Unit (EEU) The EEU is responsible for engaging with employers, liaising with academic and professional service colleagues working towards collaborative and positive outcomes. Supporting degree apprenticeships, developing and delivering Knowledge Transfer Partnerships, development and promotion of CPD programmes with employers. Supporting businesses through consultancy and contract research and providing a front door model for guidance and connection to the wider University. Read more The EEU provide advice and specialist support in the following areas: Degree Apprenticeships Knowledge Transfer Partnerships Consultancy and Research Continuous Professional Development Support for SMEs State-of-the-art resources Martin Blunt: Head of Enterprise and Engagement Unit View our main business webpage for more information, or contact us via: Telephone: +44 (0)1772 895500 Email: business@lancashire.ac.uk Online: Contact us form Ethics, Integrity and Governance Unit (EIGU) The Ethics, Integrity and Governance Unit (EIGU) is responsible for developing processes relating to Research Integrity at the University and for managing and overseeing the University ethics processes. The EIGU is also responsible for performing the role of “sponsor” of clinical research (where appropriate). The EIGU provide advice and specialist support in the following areas: Research integrity Research ethics Clinical research governance Sponsorship requirements Research involving human tissue Research involving animals International research Read more The University of Lancashire is proud to be the first European university to adopt the Global Code of Conduct for Research in Resource-Poor Settings (GCC) which is designed to prevent the export of unethical research practices to low and middle-income countries. The EIGU has an active role in the promotion of the GCC and development of processes to ensure the code is applied. Emma Law: Head of Ethics, Integrity and Governance Unit Email ethicsinfo@lancashire.ac.uk for further details. Graduate Research School (GRS) The Graduate Research School is responsible for supporting the postgraduate research environment and culture, having oversight of the student journey, as well as hosting events and activities for the PGR community. Read more We offer research skills training that is mapped to the Vitae Researcher Development Framework. We host the 3MT (Three Minute Thesis) competition and Annual PGR Conference. We deliver a range of research showcase events during the year. We support the PGR Society. We manage the University of Lancashire Undergraduate Research Internship Programme. We provide research grants to support PGR research activities. We represent the PGR community at University level. We support research supervisors and research degree tutors. We listen and respond to the PGR student voice. The University of Lancashire's postgraduate research students (PGRs) each have their own team of supervisors to support them through their research programme. More details about our postgraduate research degree programmes can be found on our Postgraduate Research page. Andrea Ferguson: Head of Graduate Research School Email GraduateSchool@lancashire.ac.uk for further details. Grants and Funding Unit (GFU) Provides support to academics from the point at which they have research ideas and are looking for funding, through identifying funding opportunities, development of proposals (including their costing and pricing), the internal approval process for submission and submission to the funders. When funding is awarded the team liaises with academics and the funder and works with the Contract team in Legal Services to ensure the contract for the project is negotiated and signed. Read more The GFU supports the academic throughout the project as a critical friend to ensure that the project is delivered, on time, to budget and to contract. The GFU supports all proposals where external funding is sought, so as well as supporting applications to research funders e.g. RCUK, NIHR, British Academy, The Royal Society, The Wellcome Trust; the Unit also provides support for applying for, or receiving funding from industries and charities. This does not have to be for research work, activities which involve consultancy work, offering a testing and analysing service, or the offer of training e.g. CPD, are also supported by the GFU. Gillian Chew: Head of Grants and Funding Unit Email GFUinfo@lancashire.ac.uk for further details. Impact and Outputs Unit (IOU) The Impact and Outputs Unit provides leadership and management for activities such as the Research Excellence Framework (REF), Knowledge Exchange Framework (KEF) and Knowledge Exchange Concordat (KEC); and the HR Excellence in Research Award and Researcher Development Concordat. The IOU provide advice and support in the following areas: Research impact Open Research Researcher development Research and KE indicators and assessment Read more The IOU supports Open Research, with the University of Lancashire research outputs and data freely accessible on our two repositories, Lancashire Online Knowledge and Lancashire Online Research Data . We also champion Responsible Research Metrics. The University of Lancashire is a signatory to the San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment. You can read the University Responsible Research Metrics statement online . The IOU also oversees researcher development activity, including the Research and Enterprise Training Programme, Research and Enterprise Induction, and responsibilities associated with the University’s HR Excellence in Research Award and Researcher Development Concordat. For more information, visit our Academic development for research and enterprise webpage . Allison McCaig: Head of Impact & Outputs Unit Email researchassessment@lancashire.ac.uk for further details. Intellectual Property & Commercialisation Unit (IPU) The IPU supports research-active staff and students in protecting intellectual property arising from their research and in commercialising their work in order to maximize impact from the University’s research whether financial, reputational and/or societal. If you are a business looking to partner with us to create commercial opportunities to license and develop intellectual property (IP), view our dedicated webpage . Read more The IPU help protect and/or commercialise ideas and research by: Providing a complete innovation roadmapto assist researchers in taking their research from the lab/classroom to the market. Managingintellectual propertyfrom disclosure, assessment, deciding on an IP protection strategy and impact/commercialisation route. This may include publishing, licensing and creating spin out companies. Providing assistance in commercialisationvia our R2M programme . Email innovationteam@lancashire.ac.uk for further details. Local and regional engagement The Service works with many regional partners on a variety of diverse projects to maximise the region’s potential for local growth and redevelopment through research, innovation and knowledge exchange. Partners cover businesses and community groups and also include the Lancashire Enterprise Partnership, Lancashire County Council and its local authorities. If you are interested in finding out more about our work, please contact Matthew Guest . Research Research and Knowledge Exchange Service (RKES) Research and Knowledge Exchange Service (RKES) Research Our skilled and knowledgeable staff provide a professional, effective and holistic offering for researchers to support them in their research and enterprise journey, from ideas and training to funding, dissemination and knowledge exchange. The service comprises six units : Enterprise and Engagement Unit (EEU) Ethics, Integrity and Governance Unit (EIGU) Graduate Research School (GRS) Grants and Funding Unit (GFU) Impact and Outputs Unit (IOU) Intellectual Property and Commercialisation Unit (IPU) Enterprise and Engagement Unit (EEU) The EEU is responsible for engaging with employers, liaising with academic and professional service colleagues working towards collaborative and positive outcomes. Supporting degree apprenticeships, developing and delivering Knowledge Transfer Partnerships, development and promotion of CPD programmes with employers. Supporting businesses through consultancy and contract research and providing a front door model for guidance and connection to the wider University. Read more The EEU provide advice and specialist support in the following areas: Degree Apprenticeships Knowledge Transfer Partnerships Consultancy and Research Continuous Professional Development Support for SMEs State-of-the-art resources Martin Blunt: Head of Enterprise and Engagement Unit View our main business webpage for more information, or contact us via: Telephone: +44 (0)1772 895500 Email: business@lancashire.ac.uk Online: Contact us form Ethics, Integrity and Governance Unit (EIGU) The Ethics, Integrity and Governance Unit (EIGU) is responsible for developing processes relating to Research Integrity at the University and for managing and overseeing the University ethics processes. The EIGU is also responsible for performing the role of “sponsor” of clinical research (where appropriate). The EIGU provide advice and specialist support in the following areas: Research integrity Research ethics Clinical research governance Sponsorship requirements Research involving human tissue Research involving animals International research Read more The University of Lancashire is proud to be the first European university to adopt the Global Code of Conduct for Research in Resource-Poor Settings (GCC) which is designed to prevent the export of unethical research practices to low and middle-income countries. The EIGU has an active role in the promotion of the GCC and development of processes to ensure the code is applied. Emma Law: Head of Ethics, Integrity and Governance Unit Email ethicsinfo@lancashire.ac.uk for further details. Graduate Research School (GRS) The Graduate Research School is responsible for supporting the postgraduate research environment and culture, having oversight of the student journey, as well as hosting events and activities for the PGR community. Read more We offer research skills training that is mapped to the Vitae Researcher Development Framework. We host the 3MT (Three Minute Thesis) competition and Annual PGR Conference. We deliver a range of research showcase events during the year. We support the PGR Society. We manage the University of Lancashire Undergraduate Research Internship Programme. We provide research grants to support PGR research activities. We represent the PGR community at University level. We support research supervisors and research degree tutors. We listen and respond to the PGR student voice. The University of Lancashire's postgraduate research students (PGRs) each have their own team of supervisors to support them through their research programme. More details about our postgraduate research degree programmes can be found on our Postgraduate Research page. Andrea Ferguson: Head of Graduate Research School Email GraduateSchool@lancashire.ac.uk for further details. Grants and Funding Unit (GFU) Provides support to academics from the point at which they have research ideas and are looking for funding, through identifying funding opportunities, development of proposals (including their costing and pricing), the internal approval process for submission and submission to the funders. When funding is awarded the team liaises with academics and the funder and works with the Contract team in Legal Services to ensure the contract for the project is negotiated and signed. Read more The GFU supports the academic throughout the project as a critical friend to ensure that the project is delivered, on time, to budget and to contract. The GFU supports all proposals where external funding is sought, so as well as supporting applications to research funders e.g. RCUK, NIHR, British Academy, The Royal Society, The Wellcome Trust; the Unit also provides support for applying for, or receiving funding from industries and charities. This does not have to be for research work, activities which involve consultancy work, offering a testing and analysing service, or the offer of training e.g. CPD, are also supported by the GFU. Gillian Chew: Head of Grants and Funding Unit Email GFUinfo@lancashire.ac.uk for further details. Impact and Outputs Unit (IOU) The Impact and Outputs Unit provides leadership and management for activities such as the Research Excellence Framework (REF), Knowledge Exchange Framework (KEF) and Knowledge Exchange Concordat (KEC); and the HR Excellence in Research Award and Researcher Development Concordat. The IOU provide advice and support in the following areas: Research impact Open Research Researcher development Research and KE indicators and assessment Read more The IOU supports Open Research, with the University of Lancashire research outputs and data freely accessible on our two repositories, Lancashire Online Knowledge and Lancashire Online Research Data . We also champion Responsible Research Metrics. The University of Lancashire is a signatory to the San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment. You can read the University Responsible Research Metrics statement online . The IOU also oversees researcher development activity, including the Research and Enterprise Training Programme, Research and Enterprise Induction, and responsibilities associated with the University’s HR Excellence in Research Award and Researcher Development Concordat. For more information, visit our Academic development for research and enterprise webpage . Allison McCaig: Head of Impact & Outputs Unit Email researchassessment@lancashire.ac.uk for further details. Intellectual Property & Commercialisation Unit (IPU) The IPU supports research-active staff and students in protecting intellectual property arising from their research and in commercialising their work in order to maximize impact from the University’s research whether financial, reputational and/or societal. If you are a business looking to partner with us to create commercial opportunities to license and develop intellectual property (IP), view our dedicated webpage . Read more The IPU help protect and/or commercialise ideas and research by: Providing a complete innovation roadmapto assist researchers in taking their research from the lab/classroom to the market. Managingintellectual propertyfrom disclosure, assessment, deciding on an IP protection strategy and impact/commercialisation route. This may include publishing, licensing and creating spin out companies. Providing assistance in commercialisationvia our R2M programme . Email innovationteam@lancashire.ac.uk for further details. Local and regional engagement The Service works with many regional partners on a variety of diverse projects to maximise the region’s potential for local growth and redevelopment through research, innovation and knowledge exchange. Partners cover businesses and community groups and also include the Lancashire Enterprise Partnership, Lancashire County Council and its local authorities. If you are interested in finding out more about our work, please contact Matthew Guest . applicants International offer holders next steps Next steps for international offer holders International applicants Congratulations, you have received an offer for your chosen course. Let us support you in taking the next important step on your journey. Meeting the academic conditions of your offer If there are academic conditions detailed in your conditional offer letter, this means that there are the documents that we still need to receive from you. The academic conditions could include a personal statement, academic reference, qualification documents or evidence of your English language qualification. Your offer might include ‘other’ conditions, which will be clearly listed, and might include the submission of an ATAS Certificate, in-country Police Check, Certificate of Good Conduct or similar. Your documents should be submitted directly to the International Admissions Team at ia@uclan.ac.uk clearly stating your University Registration Number (which appears in your offer letter) in the subject line. Paying your fees Language Academy Scholarships and bursaries Your CAS and additional offer information Open all accordion items CAS letter and student visa guidance The university is registered as a sponsor under the UK immigration system known as the Points-Based System. We will provide you with a CAS number, once you have met any academic conditions and paid the relevant tuition fee deposit. Providing evidence of any agreed sponsorship arrangements will be accepted also. You will need a CAS to be able to submit your Student visa application. Once you have paid your tuition fee deposit, we would advise that no extra tuition fee deposit payment should be submitted until your visa has been secured. Please note that all fees and costs associated with your visa application are expenses you will incur in addition to your tuition and accommodation fees. If you are coming to the UK to study for a period of more than six months there are further extra expenses. This will include the Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) . You must have enough money to pay for your course and support yourself in the UK. How much money you need depends on your circumstances. Visit the Government website for more information. Visit the student visa application guide for more information. Under 18 Student Information The University has a safeguarding responsibility toward all students and will treat all students in the same way. All students will need to have the necessary skills to study and live independently and assume an adult level of responsibility. Yet, the University acknowledges that anyone living in England who is under the age of 18 is legally defined as a child. The University will not act in “loco parentis”. This means that the University will not act in a parental capacity toward students who are under the age of 18. If your parents/guardians remain overseas when you come to study, we will ask them to provide details of a guardian based in the UK. This is the person we will contact in an emergency on your behalf should the need ever arise. The nominated UK guardian should be someone who is in or near to the University and who can act in loco parentis. The guardian must be a British national or holder of a UK Biometric Residence Permit. If you will be under the age of 18 when your course is due to begin, we will contact you after you have been issued with an offer to secure the completion of all relevant documentation. Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) Check You will be required to get a satisfactory Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) clearance if your course involves working with vulnerable groups of individuals. This information will be included within your offer letter if this requirement applies to your course. If your DBS check is unsatisfactory, your offer of a place for that course may be withdrawn. If you are an international student travelling from overseas, you should secure a letter from the local police in your home country. The UK DBS check process has no way to access information about any crimes committed overseas. Every country has its own system for criminal records checking. The terminology for the certificates may differ. Your country may refer to the process as Certificates of Good Character, rather than mentioning criminal charges which would suffice for this purpose. You should secure this evidence through the police in your home country and get a certificate either stating your current criminal record or giving an opinion on character and trustworthiness. More information about the process can be found on the Government's website. Tuition Fee Status Assessment The rules about who pays ‘home’ fees for higher education courses in England are set by the Government’s Department for Education. The regulations identify all the different ‘categories’ of students who can insist on paying the ‘home’ rate of fee. If you meet all the criteria required by any one category, including any residence requirements, we will charge you the ‘home’ fee rate. We will complete an assessment of your fee status, as required, as part of our standard application assessment process. If you believe your fee status has been categorised incorrectly, please do not hesitate to contact the International Admissions team to enable a detailed assessment to be made. Please note that the University fee assessment process is carried out independently of your application to study at it. UKCISA guidelines are considered in full when an assessment is made. A decision on your fee status is not an admission decision on your application, which will be determined separately from your fee status. Requirements for clinical courses If you have received an offer for a course that has a clinical setting, where work-based learning or a placement form part of your study, you are likely to be asked to provide additional evidence in support of your application in addition to any academic and financial conditions. The additional evidence may include a DBS Check, detailed above, and/or an Occupational Health Check. We will provide you with all the information you need at each step of your journey to enable you to provide any additional evidence requested. Please note that the UK government consultation on whether there was a requirement to be vaccinated against Covid 19 concluded the following; ‘it is no longer proportionate to require vaccination as a condition of deployment through statute in health, care homes or other social care settings.’ The university is following UK government advice and evidence of vaccination status will not be a condition of your offer. Final steps of your journey Arriving in the UK We recommend that you read our arrival guidance before travelling to the UK. This includes advice on what to bring, what to expect at the airport, and traveling to campus. Read more about Arriving in the UK Accommodation There’s something special about living in university accommodation, especially if it’s your first time away from home. With a wide range of accommodation options, we'll help you find the right place for you. Read more about Accommodation Visa advice Find out whether you need a visa, how to apply, and what documents you may need. Read more about Visa advice See more Final steps of your journey Useful contacts If you have any questions about your application or about any of the specific issues raised above, please do not hesitate to contact our dedicated teams who will be able to provide you with further assistance. applicants International offer holders next steps Next steps for international offer holders International applicants Congratulations, you have received an offer for your chosen course. Let us support you in taking the next important step on your journey. Meeting the academic conditions of your offer If there are academic conditions detailed in your conditional offer letter, this means that there are the documents that we still need to receive from you. The academic conditions could include a personal statement, academic reference, qualification documents or evidence of your English language qualification. Your offer might include ‘other’ conditions, which will be clearly listed, and might include the submission of an ATAS Certificate, in-country Police Check, Certificate of Good Conduct or similar. Your documents should be submitted directly to the International Admissions Team at ia@uclan.ac.uk clearly stating your University Registration Number (which appears in your offer letter) in the subject line. Paying your fees Language Academy Scholarships and bursaries Your CAS and additional offer information Open all accordion items CAS letter and student visa guidance The university is registered as a sponsor under the UK immigration system known as the Points-Based System. We will provide you with a CAS number, once you have met any academic conditions and paid the relevant tuition fee deposit. Providing evidence of any agreed sponsorship arrangements will be accepted also. You will need a CAS to be able to submit your Student visa application. Once you have paid your tuition fee deposit, we would advise that no extra tuition fee deposit payment should be submitted until your visa has been secured. Please note that all fees and costs associated with your visa application are expenses you will incur in addition to your tuition and accommodation fees. If you are coming to the UK to study for a period of more than six months there are further extra expenses. This will include the Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) . You must have enough money to pay for your course and support yourself in the UK. How much money you need depends on your circumstances. Visit the Government website for more information. Visit the student visa application guide for more information. Under 18 Student Information The University has a safeguarding responsibility toward all students and will treat all students in the same way. All students will need to have the necessary skills to study and live independently and assume an adult level of responsibility. Yet, the University acknowledges that anyone living in England who is under the age of 18 is legally defined as a child. The University will not act in “loco parentis”. This means that the University will not act in a parental capacity toward students who are under the age of 18. If your parents/guardians remain overseas when you come to study, we will ask them to provide details of a guardian based in the UK. This is the person we will contact in an emergency on your behalf should the need ever arise. The nominated UK guardian should be someone who is in or near to the University and who can act in loco parentis. The guardian must be a British national or holder of a UK Biometric Residence Permit. If you will be under the age of 18 when your course is due to begin, we will contact you after you have been issued with an offer to secure the completion of all relevant documentation. Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) Check You will be required to get a satisfactory Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) clearance if your course involves working with vulnerable groups of individuals. This information will be included within your offer letter if this requirement applies to your course. If your DBS check is unsatisfactory, your offer of a place for that course may be withdrawn. If you are an international student travelling from overseas, you should secure a letter from the local police in your home country. The UK DBS check process has no way to access information about any crimes committed overseas. Every country has its own system for criminal records checking. The terminology for the certificates may differ. Your country may refer to the process as Certificates of Good Character, rather than mentioning criminal charges which would suffice for this purpose. You should secure this evidence through the police in your home country and get a certificate either stating your current criminal record or giving an opinion on character and trustworthiness. More information about the process can be found on the Government's website. Tuition Fee Status Assessment The rules about who pays ‘home’ fees for higher education courses in England are set by the Government’s Department for Education. The regulations identify all the different ‘categories’ of students who can insist on paying the ‘home’ rate of fee. If you meet all the criteria required by any one category, including any residence requirements, we will charge you the ‘home’ fee rate. We will complete an assessment of your fee status, as required, as part of our standard application assessment process. If you believe your fee status has been categorised incorrectly, please do not hesitate to contact the International Admissions team to enable a detailed assessment to be made. Please note that the University fee assessment process is carried out independently of your application to study at it. UKCISA guidelines are considered in full when an assessment is made. A decision on your fee status is not an admission decision on your application, which will be determined separately from your fee status. Requirements for clinical courses If you have received an offer for a course that has a clinical setting, where work-based learning or a placement form part of your study, you are likely to be asked to provide additional evidence in support of your application in addition to any academic and financial conditions. The additional evidence may include a DBS Check, detailed above, and/or an Occupational Health Check. We will provide you with all the information you need at each step of your journey to enable you to provide any additional evidence requested. Please note that the UK government consultation on whether there was a requirement to be vaccinated against Covid 19 concluded the following; ‘it is no longer proportionate to require vaccination as a condition of deployment through statute in health, care homes or other social care settings.’ The university is following UK government advice and evidence of vaccination status will not be a condition of your offer. Final steps of your journey Arriving in the UK We recommend that you read our arrival guidance before travelling to the UK. This includes advice on what to bring, what to expect at the airport, and traveling to campus. Read more about Arriving in the UK Accommodation There’s something special about living in university accommodation, especially if it’s your first time away from home. With a wide range of accommodation options, we'll help you find the right place for you. Read more about Accommodation Visa advice Find out whether you need a visa, how to apply, and what documents you may need.
